best_for: Chromium users who want a build tuned for their CPU, with Manifest V2 extensions and extra video codecs, and who can match the right build to their processor.
description:
Thorium is a free web browser built on Chromium and named after element number 90. Its developer, Alex313031, also makes Mercury, a Firefox fork, and ThoriumOS. Each Thorium release follows Chromium's stable version while keeping its own patches and default settings, so it still feels familiar to Chrome users.

You can switch on an optional Thorium 2024 look, with see-through inactive tabs, square tabs and tab widths you set yourself. Tab Search can sit on the left or the right, Ctrl+Tab jumps to the tab you used last, the tab strip can scroll, and a tab can open to the left of the current one. Bookmark menus can spread over several columns, and internal pages open under thorium:// addresses.

points.title: Compiled for speed
points.text: Thorium is a Chromium fork built with CPU-specific instruction sets, ThinLTO and PGO. The project claims 8 to 38 percent faster results than stock Chromium, depending on benchmark and system.

points.title: Pick the build that fits your CPU
points.text: Builds range from SSE2 to AVX-512. The project warns that a build made for a feature your CPU lacks may fail before the browser opens, so check your processor first.

points.title: Keeps Manifest V2 extensions
points.text: Manifest V2 support is included, and new profiles start with uBlock Origin installed. Privacy Sandbox defaults are off and Global Privacy Control is on.

points.title: Extra codecs
points.text: It adds FFmpeg support for HEVC (H.265) and MPEG-2 video and AC-3/E-AC-3 audio, along with H.265 modes for WebRTC calls.

points.title: The Mac build lags behind
points.text: This listing shows Windows at 156.0.8078.28 but macOS at M138.0.7204.303, many Chromium releases older. Homebrew disabled the cask on 2026-09-01 because it fails Apple's Gatekeeper check.

points.title: A small team, not a big vendor
points.text: Thorium is led by one developer, Alex313031, with help on builds from contributors. It is BSD-3-Clause and free. Windows gets an x64 installer per user or per machine and a portable zip; the Windows listing keeps 14 versions, macOS only the current release.
